summary: This note is the MoveIt Humble documentation tutorial for the MoveIt Setup Assistant, a graphical tool for configuring any robot for MoveIt, whose primary function is generating an SRDF file plus other configuration files. It walks through 12 steps using the Franka Panda arm as the example, covering self-collision matrix generation, virtual joints, planning groups, robot poses, end effectors, passive joints, 3D perception, Gazebo simulation, ROS Control, author information, and generating the configuration package.
one_line: Step-by-step tutorial for using the MoveIt Setup Assistant GUI to generate SRDF and MoveIt configuration files, using the Franka Panda as the example robot.
key_facts: The MoveIt Setup Assistant is a graphical user interface for configuring any robot for use with MoveIt.
Its primary function is generating a Semantic Robot Description Format (SRDF) file for the robot.
The tutorial uses the Franka Panda robot, with the panda_arm_hand.urdf.xacro file from the Franka description package for ROS Noetic.
The Default Self-Collision Matrix Generator uses a default sampling density of 10,000 collision checks.
In Step 3, the virtual joint is named virtual_joint, with child link panda_link0, parent frame world, and joint type fixed.
The panda_arm planning group uses the kdl_kinematics_plugin/KDLKinematicsPlugin kinematics solver and spans joints from virtual_joint through panda_joint8.
The hand planning group uses the kinematic solver None and includes the links panda_hand, panda_leftfinger, and panda_rightfinger.
The end effector is named hand, with end effector group hand and parent link panda_link8.
The Panda does not have any passive joints, so the passive joints step is skipped.
The arm_position_controller uses the controller type position_controllers/JointPositionController.
The generated package is named panda_moveit_config and is created by clicking the Generate Package button in the Configuration Files pane.
Passive joints are described as unactuated joints such as passive casters that planners cannot kinematically plan for.
The Gazebo step recommends spawning the robot with rosrun gazebo_ros spawn_model using the generated URDF at position x 0, y 0, z 1.
The note is from the MoveIt Documentation Humble version, which the page describes as a stable version no longer being developed further.
